body.statement:
Let \(P_\lambda\) and \(Q_\lambda\) be probability laws dominated by \(\nu\), indexed by \(\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k)\), and let \(\mathcal Z=\bigcup_{j=1}^k\mathcal Z_j\) be a measurable partition.  Suppose \(P_\lambda(\mathcal Z_j)=Q_\lambda(\mathcal Z_j)=p_j\), and that the conditional laws on \(\mathcal Z_j\) depend only on \(\lambda_j\), with the two families differing only for \(j\in S\).  For a prior \(\varpi\), write \(\bar p=\int p_\lambda\,d\varpi(\lambda)\) and \(\bar q=\int q_\lambda\,d\varpi(\lambda)\), and define
\[
 \delta_1=\max_{j\in S}\sup_\lambda\int_{\mathcal Z_j}
 \frac{(p_\lambda-\bar p)^2}{p_\lambda p_j}\,d\nu,
 \quad
 \delta_2=\max_{j\in S}\sup_\lambda\int_{\mathcal Z_j}
 \frac{(q_\lambda-p_\lambda)^2}{p_\lambda p_j}\,d\nu,
\]
\[
 \delta_3=\max_{j\in S}\sup_\lambda\int_{\mathcal Z_j}
 \frac{(\bar q-\bar p)^2}{p_\lambda p_j}\,d\nu.
\]
If \(\bar p/p_\lambda\le b<\infty\) and \(np_j\max(1,\delta_1,\delta_2)\le b\) for every \(j\), then, for a constant \(C_b\) depending only on \(b\),
\[
 H^2\!\left(\int P_\lambda^{\otimes n}\,d\varpi(\lambda),
              \int Q_\lambda^{\otimes n}\,d\varpi(\lambda)\right)
 \le C_b n\left(\sum_{j\in S}p_j\right)
 \left[n\left(\max_{j\in S}p_j\right)
       (\delta_1\delta_2+\delta_2^2)+\delta_3\right],
\]
where \(H^2(P,Q)=\int(\sqrt{dP}-\sqrt{dQ})^2\).

source.verbatim_statement: Lemma 2. Let P_λ and Q_λ denote distributions indexed by a vector λ = (λ_1,...,λ_k), and let Z = ∪_{j=1}^k Z_j denote a partition of the sample space. Assume: 1. P_λ(Z_j) = Q_λ(Z_j) = p_j for all λ, and 2. the conditional distributions 1_{Z_j} dP_λ/p_j and 1_{Z_j} dQ_λ/p_j (given an observation is in Z_j) do not depend on λ_ℓ for ℓ ≠ j, and only differ on partitions j ∈ S ⊆ {1,...,k}. For a prior distribution ϖ over λ, let p̄ = ∫ p_λ dϖ(λ) and q̄ = ∫ q_λ dϖ(λ), and define δ_1 = max_{j∈S} sup_λ ∫_{Z_j} (p_λ-p̄)^2/(p_λ p_j) dν, δ_2 = max_{j∈S} sup_λ ∫_{Z_j} (q_λ-p_λ)^2/(p_λ p_j) dν, δ_3 = max_{j∈S} sup_λ ∫_{Z_j} (q̄-p̄)^2/(p_λ p_j) dν for a dominating measure ν. If p̄/p_λ ≤ b < ∞ and n p_j max(1,δ_1,δ_2) ≤ b for all j, then H^2(∫ P_λ^n dϖ(λ), ∫ Q_λ^n dϖ(λ)) is bounded above by C n (∑_{j∈S} p_j){n(max_{j∈S} p_j)(δ_1δ_2+δ_2^2)+δ_3} for a constant C only depending on b.

upstream.citation: James M. Robins, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen, Lingling Li, and Aad W. van der Vaart. Semiparametric minimax rates. Electronic Journal of Statistics 3:1305--1321, 2009.

body.justification: This is the published localized partition-mixture Hellinger inequality instantiated in the sign-conditioned comparison.
